title: Error Handling Strategies
learning_outcomes: Explain what error handling strategies contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: recoverable versus unrecoverable failures.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. In this lesson, focus on recoverable versus unrecoverable failures; then compare it with validation errors versus internal errors. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use error handling strategies when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. For error handling strategies, begin with recoverable versus unrecoverable failures. Also distinguish validation errors versus internal errors; appropriate exception boundaries; fail-fast principles. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for error handling strategies from top to bottom. Start by identifying recoverable versus unrecoverable failures, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
